Validated by `npm run validate:product-registry`.

products.name: Number Realm
products.tagline: A term-long math campaign where one hero levels up across every Grade 6 unit.
products.summary: A story-driven RPG that maps one realm to each Grade 6 unit. Students create a hero, battle by solving standards-aligned problems, earn XP and gold, unlock abilities, and build per-standard mastery that persists across the whole year. A Socratic in-battle Sage gives method hints without revealing answers, and a Daily Quest keeps spaced practice going between units.
products.problemSolved: Grade 6 students who have decided they are 'bad at math' stop practicing. Number Realm gives them a reason to return daily and a place where getting a problem wrong costs a little HP instead of their identity.
products.coreExperience: Choose a realm, fight through chapters by solving problems, ask the Sage for a hint, level the hero, and watch per-standard mastery climb.
differentiators: One persistent hero across all ten units, not ten disconnected minigames.
Socratic hints that teach a method and never hand over the answer.
Per-standard mastery tiers that map directly onto the curriculum's standards registry.
Fully offline-capable static HTML — no login, no account, no student PII.
implementationRequirements: Any modern browser, including school Chromebooks.
Works offline once loaded; the optional AI Sage endpoint degrades to built-in method hints when unavailable.
manualEvidenceNeeded: Consented student work samples or gameplay screenshots.
A short demonstration recording of a battle plus a Sage hint.
Classroom usage data, if the teacher chooses to collect and share it.
limitations: Cross-device resume needs the optional save/resume backend enabled; without it, progress is per-device.
The AI Sage requires the /api/tutor endpoint. When it is offline the game falls back to each problem's built-in method hint.
No published efficacy study exists for this product.

products.name: Language Bridge
products.tagline: Grade-level mathematics with the language barrier removed, not the math.
products.summary: The platform-wide language-access layer: bilingual vocabulary and audio, a five-rung writing scaffold ladder, read-aloud, language objectives on every lesson, and family-facing explanations in home languages. It is a view across the curriculum's existing supports rather than a separate ESOL program, so a multilingual learner works the same grade-level problem as everyone else.
products.problemSolved: Multilingual learners are routinely handed easier mathematics instead of more accessible language. Language Bridge changes what a task asks students to read and write, never what it asks them to understand mathematically.
products.coreExperience: Pick the supports you need, keep them across every lesson and game, and answer the same grade-level question with the amount of writing scaffold you actually need today.
differentiators: The mathematical learning target is identical at every rung of the scaffold ladder.
Supports follow the learner across lessons, games, projects, and progress views instead of resetting per activity.
Language objectives are registry data, so lesson pages, teacher views, and family summaries cannot drift apart.
Family-facing material reuses the existing Family Connections surface — no second parent portal or login.
implementationRequirements: No account required. Support selections persist in the browser.
Read-aloud uses the browser's built-in speech synthesis; availability varies by device and voice pack.
manualEvidenceNeeded: Native-speaker review of the Spanish translations already in the vocabulary manifest.
Consented family feedback on the home-language summaries.
A formal WIDA-alignment review before any WIDA claim is expanded.
limitations: Spanish is the only home language with translated vocabulary and family copy today; other languages fall back to English with read-aloud and visual supports.
Translations are teacher-authored and have not had an external translation review.
No WIDA endorsement or certification is claimed. Specific features are mapped to WIDA descriptors; the product is not WIDA-certified.

products.name: Design Studio
products.tagline: Real design challenges where the mathematics decides whether the plan works.
products.summary: A curated project layer over the existing culminating projects, Architect challenges, Start-Up City capstone, Math Workbench modeling tools, and Evidence Studio. Every project runs the same eleven-step flow — choose, brief, constraints, plan, build, calculate, test, revise, defend, save, present — and lands in the student's existing portfolio with standards and revision history attached.
products.problemSolved: Most 'project-based' math tasks are worksheets with a picture on top: the student choice never changes the answer. Design Studio projects vary dimensions, budgets, materials, and customers, so two students who choose differently must compute differently.
products.coreExperience: Take a design brief with real constraints, model it, compute it, test it, revise it, and defend the result with mathematical evidence in your portfolio.
differentiators: Student choices change the mathematics, not just the colors.
A single consistent project flow across short Architect challenges, unit capstones, and the year-end Start-Up City.
Revision history and mathematical defense are first-class portfolio artifacts, not afterthoughts.
Presentation mode hides the editing UI and shows problem, process, revisions, math, product, and reflection.
implementationRequirements: Browser only. Printing or exporting a portfolio entry is an explicit student action.
Some 3D modeling widgets need WebGL; each has a 2D fallback.
manualEvidenceNeeded: Consented student project artifacts for a public gallery.
Teacher-scored rubric samples showing the range of student solutions.
limitations: Portfolio entries live in the browser. A student who clears site data loses them unless they exported first.
Peer feedback is captured in-page and is not routed between devices.

products.name: Personalized Math Path
products.tagline: Every recommendation says out loud why it was chosen.
products.summary: A transparent, rules-based instructional loop connecting the existing confidence checks, My Math Progress, Insight Brief, Resource Finder, and Close the Loop. Learning evidence identifies a specific instructional need, the need is matched to a real resource in the curriculum registry, and the follow-up evidence decides whether the intervention actually worked.
products.problemSolved: Adaptive systems usually hand a student a task with no explanation and hand a teacher a score with no diagnosis. This loop names the reason — prerequisite gap, vocabulary barrier, calculation slip, low confidence despite correct work — in language a sixth grader can read.
products.coreExperience: Rate your confidence, do the work, and get one next step with a plain-language reason attached to it.
differentiators: Rules-based and inspectable: every recommendation exposes the signals that produced it.
Distinguishes nine distinct instructional needs rather than a single 'struggling' flag.
Reads the same on-device learning signal the teacher's Insight Brief reads, so student and teacher never see contradictory advice.
Reuses the existing progress surfaces instead of adding another dashboard.
implementationRequirements: Recommendations improve as evidence accumulates; a brand-new learner gets a neutral starting path.
No server or model call is required — the rules run in the browser.
manualEvidenceNeeded: Teacher review of whether the stated reasons match their professional read of each student.
Longitudinal data showing whether recommended interventions changed outcomes.
limitations: The loop can only reason about activities that report evidence; a paper task is invisible to it.
Recommendation quality has not been externally validated.
'Improvement after a recommendation' needs at least one follow-up attempt on the same standard before it reports anything.

products.name: Grade 6 Curriculum System
products.tagline: A complete Grade 6 mathematics curriculum organized around the decision a teacher is actually making.
products.summary: The platform itself: ten units and the full lesson library, each lesson carrying its standard, learning target, language objective, vocabulary, guided notes, slides, homework, printables, family page, and teacher notes. The hub is organized by decision — Teach Today, Plan the Week, Explore by Unit, Teacher Tools, Classroom Experiences, Full Unit Directory — rather than by file type.
products.problemSolved: Curriculum sites are usually organized the way the files were stored, so a teacher with eleven minutes before class has to go hunting. This one opens on the decision they are making right now.
products.coreExperience: Open the hub, land on today's lesson with everything attached, and reach any other lesson, resource, or tool in one or two clicks.
differentiators: Decision-first information architecture instead of a file-type directory.
One canonical registry behind every unit title, standard, learning target, and language objective on the site.
Every lesson ships the full teaching set, not just slides.
Static and offline-friendly: no login wall between a student and a lesson.
implementationRequirements: Static hosting. No database is required for the core curriculum.
Optional Cloudflare D1 backends add cross-device progress and roster features.
manualEvidenceNeeded: Adoption or usage data beyond the author's own classroom.
limitations: Built and maintained for one Grade 6 classroom; it has not been piloted at district scale.
Standards are coded to the 2025 Maryland MCCRS codes, with a CCSS crosswalk provided for other states.

products.name: Teacher Studio
products.tagline: From a standard to a reviewed, classroom-ready resource — with the review steps built in.
products.summary: A guided workflow that connects the existing teacher tools into one ordered path: choose a unit, lesson, or standard; pick what you need; generate or locate it from approved curriculum data; run mathematical, answer-key, accessibility, and ESOL checks; edit; export; and register the result back into the curriculum. The underlying tools are unchanged — Teacher Studio orders them and adds the human-review checkpoints.
products.problemSolved: Generated instructional material tends to ship unreviewed. Teacher Studio makes the validation and human-approval steps part of the path instead of something a busy teacher is expected to remember.
products.coreExperience: Start from a standard, walk ten ordered steps, and finish with a resource that has passed math, answer-key, accessibility, and language review before any student sees it.
differentiators: Generated content cannot auto-publish; a teacher review checkpoint is a required step.
Every generator is constrained to the canonical curriculum registry, so a new resource cannot invent a conflicting unit title or standard.
Organizes tools that already work rather than rebuilding them on one screen.
Ends by registering the resource, which keeps the curriculum registry and the site in sync.
implementationRequirements: Roster and gradebook views require the existing teacher key; without it the workflow still runs on curriculum data alone.
Repository build and packaging scripts are workstation tools and are intentionally not runnable from the published site.
manualEvidenceNeeded: Teacher testimony about time saved, gathered with consent.
Samples of resources that passed and failed each review gate.
limitations: The validation steps are structural and rule-based; they surface likely problems and do not replace a teacher's mathematical judgment.
Registering a resource writes to repository data and therefore completes on a maintainer workstation, not in the browser.
